## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shòuchí qī fó mínghào suǒshēng gōngdé jīng* is a brief single-fascicle sūtra enumerating the merit accruing to those who uphold the names of seven named Buddhas. It is related thematically to the Yakushi (Bhaiṣajyaguru / Medicine Buddha) sūtra cycle, in that the seven Buddhas praised here may overlap with the seven Medicine Buddhas of the expanded *Yakushi* tradition (cf. [KR6i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0049)). The translator colophon reads: 大唐三藏法師玄奘奉詔譯 ("Translated by the Tripiṭaka master [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) of the Great Táng, by imperial command"). [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (602–664 CE) was the foremost Táng-dynasty translator and the monk responsible for the definitive Chinese translation of the *Bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra* (T14n0450 = [KR6i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0048)).

**Abstract**

The *Shòuchí qī fó mínghào jīng* is a compact listing of seven Buddhas with their meritorious qualities, translated by [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) during his active period as court translator (649–664 CE). The text participates in the broader "seven Buddhas" devotional tradition that includes the *Ratanasutta* (Pāli) and the various iterations of the *Bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra* that list seven Medicine Buddhas. The specific seven Buddhas named here may differ from those in the seven-Yakushi tradition; establishing the exact relationship would require a philological comparison of this text with T14n0451 ([KR6i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0049)). The translation's provenance under imperial commission (*fèngzhào*) is typical of his later translation work at the court-sponsored translation academy.
